items: 400g mixed mushrooms, such as oyster, shiitake, button, lion’s mane, chestnut
a few sprigs of fresh coriander

steps: Drizzle 1 tablespoon of olive oil into the base of a cold large non-stick frying pan, then season generously with sea salt and black pepper. Halve or quarter the mushrooms, leaving some whole so you get a mix of sizes, then arrange in the pan in an even layer.
Place a large plate or a lid that’s smaller than the pan directly onto the mushrooms. Cook on medium heat for 15 minutes without stirring, checking occasionally to avoid burning.

Place the rice and 2 mugs (600ml) of boiling kettle water in a medium non-stick saucepan. Peel the ginger, add the trimmings to the pan, season with salt, then cook with the lid on for 12 minutes, or until the rice is tender and the water absorbed.
Peel and cut the onion into chunky 1cm rounds. Trim, deseed and halve the chillies lengthways. Peel the garlic. Trim and finely chop the lemongrass, then slice the peeled ginger.

Remove the mushrooms to a board. Wipe the pan and return to medium heat. Dry fry the onion rounds, chilli, garlic and ginger for 10 minutes, until charred and fragrant, adding the whole tomatoes, lime leaves and lemongrass halfway.
For crispy rice, once no water is visible in the pan, turn the heat up to medium-high and cook with the lid off for 5 minutes, until golden and crisp on the bottom.

Add the honey, balsamic and curry powder to the charred veg and cook 1 minute. Transfer to a blender with the desiccated coconut, coconut milk and soy sauce. Blitz until smooth, then return to the pan with most of the cashew nuts. Season to taste.

Roughly chop half the mushrooms, leave the rest whole, then stir into the sauce. Pick over coriander leaves, sprinkle the reserved cashews on top and swirl over any remaining coconut milk from the tin. Tip out the rice, grate over lime zest and serve with lime wedges.
Source: Jamie Oliver — Mighty mushroom curry.[1]
